content:
The test image shows a corn ear with orange/yellow kernels covered in dark green to gray-green mold growing between and on the kernels. This points to an ear rot disease. The dark blue-green coloration between kernels strongly suggests Trichoderma Ear Rot.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows Trichoderma Ear Rot with dark green to gray-green mold on husk leaves. The test image shows the same dark green mold growing between the corn kernels directly on the ear — matching the description of "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels."

Key matching features:
- Dark green/gray-green mold between kernels (characteristic Trichoderma coloration)
- Orange/yellow kernels still visible underneath
- Mold distributed across the ear surface
- Not pink/red (rules out Gibberella/Fusarium), not olive-green powdery (rules out Aspergillus), not white at base (rules out Diplodia)
